lesson.title: Justice and democratic processes
lesson.summary: Distinguish judicial assistance and voter influence from narrowly described administrative functions.

prerequisites.reason: The learner must distinguish the listed-use enquiry from the product route.

blocks: The **justice use** in point 8(a) concerns AI used by a judicial authority or on its behalf to help research/interpret facts and law and apply law to concrete facts, or similarly in alternative dispute resolution.
A fictional decision assistant suggesting how law applies to a case differs from a tool only booking meeting rooms. The actual decision-related purpose needs evidence.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Annex III 8(a), 8(b); Article 6(2), 6(3)

blocks: The **election-influence use** in point 8(b) concerns influencing election/referendum outcomes or people's voting behaviour when exercising their vote.

Targeted voter persuasion is different from organising a campaign's internal calendar. The exclusion describes tools whose outputs people are not directly exposed to, such as administrative/logistical campaign organisation.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Annex III 8(a), 8(b); Article 6(2), 6(3)

blocks: Examine both intended function and who encounters the output. A campaign tool beginning as internal scheduling may later generate messages directly shown to voters.

Do not infer the administrative exclusion merely from the customer being a campaign organisation. A tool supporting interpretation in a judicial case similarly differs from general administrative support.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Annex III 8(a), 8(b); Article 6(2), 6(3)

blocks: Northbridge's fictional public-decision clinic records the exact point and boundary. The evidence should show whether outputs assist case reasoning or directly influence voters, not just the platform's customer category.
Then complete paragraph 3, profiling, prohibition, scope, other-law and date analyses. Neither a judge's review nor a logistical label automatically supplies an exemption.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Annex III 8(a), 8(b); Article 6(2), 6(3)
